title: Deterministic cellular-automaton models of Peña et al. and 't Hooft
html:
Remark. Deterministic cellular-automaton models of Peña et al. and 't Hooft

Remark (Relation to Peña et al. and 't Hooft). Peña et al. construct a reversible quantum Game of Life using Toffoli-based adder circuits. Their Toffoli gate is the classical limit q \to 1 of the q-Toffoli, and their construction is recovered in that limit; away from it the two are not comparable, since the q-deformed generator is invertible but not unitary. Their unitary tick maps to 3 Planck steps. We identify the q-deformed amplitude P_{7,6}(q) as the physical AND amplitude. In the canonical convention z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) it has a single zero on q > 0, at q = 1, and the diagonal P_{7,7}^{D} has none. The well-definedness condition — the diagonal positive and the q-AND non-vanishing — therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate; the one excluded point is the classical limit itself, where the q-deformation contributes nothing. The three operator zeros once quoted here — q_\star = 1/\varphi^{2}, q_\Phi \approx 0.4656, and q = 1 — belong to the excised convention C; only the last survives the change of convention.

The relation to 't Hooft's proposal — that quantum mechanics emerges from a deterministic Planck-scale cellular automaton — is more limited, and the limitation is structural rather than a matter of detail. The mechanism 't Hooft relies on is that a deterministic evolution permutes a distinguished basis of ontological states, so that the operator it induces on the span of that basis is automatically unitary and generates a Schrödinger flow. That step requires unitarity of the tick, and by the statement's item 4 the q-Toffoli is unitary only at q = 1.

Consequently the identification holds at q = 1 and is not established away from it. At q = 1 the tick is a permutation of basis states, the ontological states may be read as Reeb bundle fibres \mathcal{S}_p and the tick as the Planck step t_P(q) — but q = 1 is also where the q-Toffoli degenerates to the ordinary Toffoli gate, so what the classical limit realizes is the construction of Peña et al. rather than anything the q-deformation contributes. At q \neq 1 the tick remains invertible, and the automaton remains deterministic and reversible in the sense a cellular automaton requires, but the induced operator is not unitary and 't Hooft's embedding does not apply as stated. Whether a deterministic automaton with an invertible non-unitary tick can support the emergence 't Hooft argues for is not addressed here.

The reading of the Markov trace as a categorical coarse-graining replacing 't Hooft's information loss is likewise not established. It is a suggestion the degeneracy of the trace form makes worth examining — a degenerate form has a radical, and quotienting by a radical is a loss of information rather than an ad hoc postulate of one — but no such identification is derived in this paper. The amplitude is written P_{7,6} rather than \Phi, which is retired as an object rather than re-derived (Toffoli transfer matrix); the renaming changes no criterion and no number.
